description.value: This pilot study examined associations between cannabis use and brain structure in adults aged 60 years and older using structural MRI, with group comparisons adjusted for age and depression symptoms.

spans.text: This pilot study assessed structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in adults 60 years and older who were either current cannabis users or nonusers.

description.value: The study was cross-sectional and compared older adult cannabis users with nonusers.

spans.text: However, this study was exploratory and impacted by important limitations, most importantly in that it was cross-sectional.

Adults aged 60 years and older who reported consuming cannabis at least once per week for at least the last year ( n = 28) or who reported never using cannabis ( n = 28) were recruited from the Boulder-Denver metro through online advertisements and direct mail flyers.
This study compared overall brain structure and cortical and subcortical gray matter between adults 60 years and older who were current cannabis users or nonusers.
